name: Capstone — The Investor Data Room
goal: Ship five documented, re-runnable SQL deliverables that survive a PE firm's diligence — then present them to leadership.

brief.from: Arjun Mehta · CFO — "This is the one"
brief.body: The PE firm's data team sent their due-diligence checklist. They don't want a deck — they want clean, documented SQL outputs they can re-run themselves. Five deliverables. I'm not telling you how to write any of them — you've built every piece across the last five sprints. Each must be commented, formatted, handle the edge cases we found, and come with a two-line business interpretation. Then you present to me and Priya. Don't embarrass us.

clinic.title: Capstone rules — graded like a real deliverable
clinic.body: Only DR-1 is built together; DR-2…DR-5 are yours. Every query must (1) use customers_clean, (2) be net of returns where money is involved, (3) guard divide-by-zero, (4) account for the orphans/deprecated SKUs from Sprint 3, and (5) carry comments + a 2-line interpretation. A correct number with no documentation is a partial pass. These deliverables are self-marked here — write the SQL in the scratch box, run it, and record your interpretation in the notes.

classwork.title: Build DR-1 together — set the documentation bar

steps.instr: DR-1 · Revenue Quality by Category & Quarter. Note the documentation header — that bar applies to all five.
steps.sql:
-- ============================================================
-- INVESTOR DATA ROOM · DR-1 · Revenue Quality by Category & Quarter
-- Purpose: net revenue (after returns), margin, and QoQ growth
-- Edge cases: returns zeroed (not deleted); divide-by-zero guarded
-- ============================================================
WITH quarterly AS (
  SELECT o.Category, o.OrderYear, o.OrderQuarter,
    ROUND(SUM(o.Revenue),0) AS gross_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 0 ELSE o.Revenue END),0) AS net_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN o.ReturnFlag='Yes' THEN 0 ELSE o.GrossProfit END),0) AS net_profit
  FROM orders o GROUP BY o.Category, o.OrderYear, o.OrderQuarter)
SELECT Category, OrderQuarter AS period, gross_revenue, net_revenue,
  gross_revenue - net_revenue AS revenue_lost_to_returns,
  ROUND(net_profit/NULLIF(net_revenue,0)*100,2) AS net_margin_pct,
  ROUND((net_revenue - LAG(net_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY Category ORDER BY OrderYear, OrderQuarter))
        /NULLIF(LAG(net_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY Category ORDER BY OrderYear, OrderQuarter),0)*100,1) AS qoq_growth_pct
FROM quarterly ORDER BY Category, OrderYear, OrderQuarter;
steps.checkpoint: Interpretation (2 lines): name the fastest-growing category and the one whose margin is eroding. That's what an investor reads first.

classwork.reference: -- DR-1 as above. Note: ShopNow's OrderQuarter is already 'Q1-2022' style, so it is the period label; ordering by (OrderYear, OrderQuarter) is chronologically correct.

tickets.title: Customer Health Scorecard
tickets.prompt: LTV tiers, revenue concentration %, average orders, segment breakdown, and win-back exposure (good customers gone quiet). Design it yourself, drawing on SHOP-401/402 + SHOP-4S. Write the SQL in the scratch box, run it, and record your findings + interpretation in the notes.
acceptanceCriteria: Builds on SHOP-401/402 + SHOP-4S (LTV tiers + win-back)
tickets.modelNote: No reference solution — this is your capstone. What good looks like: a tier table with an explicit 'top tiers = X% of revenue' sentence, plus a win-back count/₹ exposure. Lead your interpretation with the concentration number.

tickets.title: Regional & Returns Risk
tickets.prompt: Return and cancellation rates by region ranked against the national average, plus subcategory return hotspots with revenue at risk. Draw on SHOP-202 + SHOP-2S. Write, run, and interpret.
acceptanceCriteria: Ranks regions vs the national benchmark (window or subquery)
tickets.modelNote: What good looks like: each region's return rate next to the national average with a rank, and the top subcategory hotspots with ₹ at risk. Remember 'Unknown' region rows must appear, not vanish.

tickets.title: Cash Reconciliation Statement
tickets.prompt: The diligence-winner: total order revenue vs total cash collected, with every rupee of the gap explained (orphans, unpaid orders, partial refunds, deprecated SKUs). Draw on the Sprint 3 classwork + SHOP-301. Write, run, and interpret.
acceptanceCriteria: Builds on the Sprint 3 reconciliation + SHOP-301
One reconciling statement: revenue - collected = sum of explained components
Every component a labelled line with count + ₹
tickets.modelNote: What good looks like: a single labelled statement where the components (orphan payments, unpaid orders, matched-amount gaps) sum to the total gap — no unexplained residual. This is the number the PE firm scrutinises hardest.

tickets.title: Growth & Funnel Story
tickets.prompt: MoM revenue trajectory with growth %, a retention cohort summary, and the web funnel conversion — the forward-looking narrative. Draw on SHOP-501 + the Sprint 5 cohort classwork + SHOP-5S. Write, run, and interpret.
acceptanceCriteria: Builds on SHOP-501 + cohort classwork + SHOP-5S
Funnel built on the cleaned clickstream (dedup + normalised)
One slide-ready summary of trend, retention shape, biggest funnel leak
tickets.modelNote: What good looks like: the revenue trend and its inflection, the retention curve's shape (where cohorts drop off), and the funnel's single biggest leak — named as the top growth opportunity.

finalReview.title: Final Review — present to leadership
finalReview.body: 10 minutes with Arjun and Priya. Not a code walkthrough — a findings presentation: revenue quality & growth, customer concentration & risk, the reconciliation result, and the single biggest opportunity and biggest risk you'd flag to investors. Expect pushback — 'is that net of returns?', 'did you dedupe?', 'what about the orphan payments?'. Surviving the questions is the assessment.
